chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, saying: Abdullah ibn Jibla narrated to us from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'If the Qa'im arises, people will deny him because he returns to them as a young man, successful, and none will remain steadfast with him except a believer whom Allah has taken a covenant from in the first Creation.'
ai.seo_question: Why will people deny Imam al-Mahdi when he reappears?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the psychological barrier of 'youthful appearance' during the Major Occultation, where prolonged absence leads the masses to expect an aged leader, causing them to reject the Mahdi when he returns as a young man. It underscores the distinction between superficial recognition and deep spiritual fidelity, linking the steadfastness of true believers to the primordial covenant (*Dahr al-Dhurr*) mentioned in Shia exegesis. This narrative serves to validate the continuity of the Imamate despite the disorientation caused by the long occultation (*al-Ghayba al-Kubra*).
